context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
context.conclusion: dimH(Feuc)=dimH(E)+1, with Feuc in Euclidean Wn and E in Euclidean Vn.

record.type: extended diameter, for subsets of a pseudo extended metric space
record.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y): x∈B, y∈B} in [0,∞], with sup ∅=0.

record.type: real diameter notation for subsets of a metric space
record.definition: For a metric space Z and B⊆Z, diam(B)=(ediam(B)).toReal, where toReal agrees with finite nonnegative reals and sends ∞ to 0. Only finite-extended-diameter sets are assigned real diameters in our covering arguments. Empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

record.type: extended nonnegative content C_p(r,B), also denoted YuiContent p r B
record.definition: For a metric (or extended metric) space Z, real p, r∈[0,∞], B⊆Z, define C_p(r,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} ∑_{i≥0} sup_{h:U_i≠∅}(ediam(U_i))^p. Empty infima are ∞ and empty suprema are 0. Thus empty cover members cost zero, also at p=0. This is exactly YuiContent in basis-registry.json/lean_header. For a real scale δ≥0, C_p(δ,B) means C_p(ofReal δ,B); nonnegative real finite costs are embedded in [0,∞]. Throughout, a δ-cover means a family covering the set with ediam of every member ≤ofReal δ; the finite-scale real-diameter notation never admits an unbounded member through toReal(∞)=0.

record.type: unnormalized diameter-power Hausdorff measure μH[p] on Borel extended metric spaces
record.definition: μH[p] is the native unnormalized Hausdorff measure, MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure p = Measure.mkMetric (r↦r^p). Its underlying outer measure is obtained from the metric outer measure construction: at each positive scale infimize the sums of diameter powers of countable covers, empty members costing zero, then take the supremum as the scale tends to zero. Evaluation μH[p](B) is the outer-measure value on any B⊆Z, with no measurability assumption on B. Explicitly, μH[p](B)=sup_{r∈[0,∞],r>0} C_p(r,B), including all extended positive scales.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

record.definition: For an extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, dimH(B)=sup{a∈[0,∞): μH[a](B)=∞}, evaluated in [0,∞] using the Borel measurable structure. The supremum of an empty set of exponents is 0. This is the native Hausdorff dimension with the original critical-exponent convention; the equality of the native measure and the original positive-exponent covering normalization is established in the proof.

For metric spaces Z,Y, maxProd(Z,Y) is Z×Y with distance between (x,t),(y,u) equal to max(dist_Z(x,y),dist_Y(t,u)). For real normed spaces this is the standard max norm on the product. Products in auxiliary propositions use this metric unless explicitly Euclidean.

record.type: Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with its Borel measurable structure
record.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, whose values on arbitrary subsets mean its outer-measure values. For a measurable space Z, measure ν and B⊆Z, ν|B denotes the restricted measure; on measurable S it has value ν(S∩B).
For B⊆Z, indicator(B)(t)=1 when t∈B and 0 otherwise; w indicator(B) is the function equal to w on B and 0 off B, for w∈[0,∞], including w=∞.

For a measure ν on a measurable space Z and f:Z→[0,∞], lintegral_ν(f)=∫⁻ f dν is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded pointwise by f. The integral of a simple function is the finite sum of its distinct nonzero values times the measure of the corresponding fibers. ∫⁻_B f dν means lintegral_{ν|B}(f).
For a finite dimensional real vector space Z, finrank(Z)=Module.finrank ℝ Z is the natural-number cardinality of any finite basis. Natural values are embedded into [0,∞] in dimension inequalities.
For a metric space Z, center u∈Z and radius a∈ℝ, closedBall(u,a)={x∈Z: dist(x,u)≤a}.
Vn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), identified with ℝ^n with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. Fin n={0,...,n−1}; for n=0 it is empty and Vn consists of the zero tuple.
Wn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(n+1)), with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure.

T(x,t) has coordinates T(x,t)(i.castSucc)=x(i) for i∈Fin n and T(x,t)(Fin.last n)=t, where i.castSucc retains the index i<n in Fin(n+1) and Fin.last n is its last index n. This defines a total map without presupposing linearity or invertibility.
Feuc={z∈Wn : (i↦z(i.castSucc))∈E and z(Fin.last n)∈I}. This is exactly the Euclidean product subset E×[0,1] in the original target.

record.type: original unnormalized positive-exponent Hausdorff content H^p_δ(A), valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: For a metric space Z, A⊆Z, real p>0 and finite real δ>0, Hscale(p,δ,A), also written H^p_δ(A), is inf{∑_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^p : A⊆⋃_{i≥0}U_i, and diam U_i≤δ for all i}. Here admissible members U_i are bounded subsets of Z; their ordinary diameter is sup{dist(x,y): x,y∈U_i} in [0,∞), with diameter of ∅ equal to zero. Equivalently the memberwise admissibility condition is dist(x,y)≤δ for every x,y in each U_i. Covers are countable, represented by ℕ-indexed families, with finite covers padded by ∅, and each empty member contributes zero. No measurability, openness, or intersection-with-A restriction is imposed on cover members. All sums and infima are taken in [0,∞], and an infimum over no admissible cover is ∞. In Euclidean Z this is precisely the original formula and conventions of problem.md:34–43; the same formula defines its metric-space extension. The cutoff is ≤δ, and there is no multiplicative dimensional normalization.

record.type: original unnormalized positive-exponent Hausdorff measure H^p(A), valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: For a metric space Z, A⊆Z and real p>0, Hmeasure(p,A), also written H^p(A), is sup_{δ∈ℝ, δ>0} Hscale(p,δ,A). This is the original H^p(A)=sup_{δ>0} H^p_δ(A) of problem.md:34–43, using exactly D018's countable covers, empty-member costs and cutoff convention. It has no multiplicative normalization and is defined on every subset A, without a measurability requirement. On general metric spaces we use this same formula as the extension of the supplied Euclidean definition.

record.statement: For every extended metric space Z with measurable structure equal to its Borel structure, every p∈ℝ and B⊆Z, μH[p](B)=sup_{r∈[0,∞], r>0} C_p(r,B). record.statement: For every metric space X with its Borel structure, A⊆X and real p>0, at each finite positive real scale δ, C_p(δ,A) is exactly the infimum of ∑_i diam(U_i)^p over countable δ-covers of A, with empty members costing zero. Each cover bounds content above. It is antitone in δ; μH[p](A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_p(δ,A). Moreover μH[p](A)=0 iff for every δ>0 and ε>0 an admissible ℕ-indexed cover has cost <ε. Suprema along scales decreasing to zero give the same measure. These agree exactly with the original H^p_δ and H^p, without a normalization factor. Countable subfamilies and pairs (i,j) with j<N_i may be enumerated by ℕ and padded by empty sets without changing coverage or nonnegative cost.

record.statement: For every metric space X, A⊆X and real q>0, if μH[q](A)=0 then μH[q+1](A×I)=0 in maxProd(X,ℝ). Under the same premise μH[q](A)=0, more precisely, for every 0<r≤1 and ε>0 there is a countable cover of A×I of diameter at most 2r and total (q+1)-cost <2^(q+2)ε (hence also ≤ that bound). The constant depends only on q.

For every metric space X with its Borel structure, A⊆X, real s>0 and finite real δ>0, C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I) in maxProd(X,ℝ); consequently μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I). These inequalities hold in [0,∞] even when C_s(δ,A)=∞ and without any measurability, compactness or nonemptiness assumption on A or the cover members.
For every finite dimensional real normed space V and A⊆V, 0≤dimH(A)≤finrank(V)<∞. In particular dimH(A) is a finite nonnegative real viewed in [0,∞], including when finrank(V)=0.

For the original natural n, the coordinate map T:maxProd(Vn,ℝ)→Wn is a real linear equivalence with inverse z↦((i↦z(i.castSucc)),z(Fin.last n)). It maps Fmax exactly onto Feuc, and dimH(Feuc)=dimH(Fmax). For all x,y∈Vn and t,u∈ℝ, setting a=||x−y||₂ and b=|t−u| gives domain distance max(a,b) and target distance sqrt(a²+b²), with max(a,b)≤sqrt(a²+b²)≤sqrt(2)max(a,b). The constants are independent of n,E and points, and all assertions include n=0.
